title: Independence of the compactification and the cocycle condition
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible and $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type with $Y$
qcqs. For compactifications $c_a=(j_a:X\to Z_a,\ p_a:Z_a\to Y)$ write
$Rf_!^{c_a}=Rp_{a*}j_{a!}$ on $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. For any two
compactifications $c_1,c_2$ there is an isomorphism
$\phi_{c_2,c_1}:Rf_!^{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^{c_2}$, obtained from the
refinement isomorphisms through any common dense refinement, which is
independent of the common refinement chosen and satisfies
$\phi_{c,c}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\phi_{c_3,c_2}\circ\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\phi_{c_3,c_1}$.

proof.text: Put $F_c=Rp_*j_!$. The candidate is the composite on the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module objects, as in [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification]. Restrict its source to the indicated localizing category and retain the ambient target $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$; preservation of the target localizing category is not required for this comparison theorem. Throughout use the canonical comparison $R(ph)_*\simeq Rp_*Rh_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied to the pro-etale ringed topoi with the pulled-back coefficient sheaves. These are the module pushforwards of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Their inverse images are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so their direct images preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Consequently all the comparisons for a string of proper maps can be computed on the same K-injective complex: both parenthesizations identify with the successive underived direct images of that complex. The underived comparison is the sheaf composition comparison of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]; at a site object its two triple composites both use the canonical identification with the same iterated fibre product. Thus these derived comparisons have the identity and associativity normalizations. No completed or common-stage coefficient category is substituted for the ordinary module-object category.

source.place: Proof, Refinement isomorphisms: derived direct-image identifications; Stacks Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition

proof.text: Let $h:c'\to c$ be a refinement with $c'$ scheme-theoretically dense; $c$ need not be dense. Apply [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange] with its proper map $p=\operatorname{id}_X$, its open immersion $i=j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, and its dense compactification $(j':X\hookrightarrow Z',r=h)$ of $j\circ\operatorname{id}_X$. All its hypotheses hold: $j$ is quasi-compact by the definition of compactification, $h$ is proper and $hj'=j$, and $j'$ is dense. Clauses (2) and (3), using $R\operatorname{id}_*\simeq\operatorname{id}$, give $e_h:j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*j'_!K$ for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$, uniquely characterized by restriction to $\operatorname{id}_K$. These maps are natural in $K$: the exact open adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] induces the derived adjunction by the exact-functor and derived-adjunction clauses of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; $e_h$ is the adjoint of the natural restriction identification with $K$. In particular, when both compactifications are dense this is exactly the map of [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement], by its clause (1). This establishes the comparison with arbitrary $c$ directly; the Noetherian closure-normalization lemma is not used.

source.place: Proof, Dense replacement and Refinement isomorphisms; replace the unsupported Noetherian reduction by the identity-proper-map specialization of det-sf-comp-composition-interchange

proof.text: We record explicitly the restriction normalization used in composing these maps. Suppose $h^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)$ and $h|_X=\operatorname{id}_X$. For a sheaf $M$ on $Z'$, restriction of $h_*M$ to an object $V\to X$ is $M(V\times_ZZ')=M(V)$ on the copy of $X$ in $Z'$: this is the base-change formula of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], lifted with the same coefficient action by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Hence $j^*h_*=j'^*$, with its canonical identification. For a K-injective resolution $I$ of a complex on $Z'$, $j'^*I$ is K-injective because $j'^*$ is right adjoint to the exact $j'_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Exact restriction therefore gives $j^*Rh_*\simeq j'^*$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. Applying the same calculation to successive maps restricts each to the identity on $X$, so these restriction identifications commute with the derived composition comparison of Step 1.

source.place: Proof, Refinement isomorphisms and Independence: restriction of composites to X

proof.text: For $h:c'\to c$ with $c'$ dense define $\rho_h:F_c\to F_{c'}$ by applying $Rp_*$ to $e_h$ and then the inverse of the composition comparison of Step 1. It is a natural isomorphism. If $k:c''\to c'$ is a further refinement with $c''$ dense, the two maps $e_{hk}$ and $Rh_*(e_k)\circ e_h$ from $j_!K$ to $R(hk)_*j''_!K$ restrict to $\operatorname{id}_K$, by Step 3. Clause (2) of [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange], applied with $p=\operatorname{id}_X$, $i=j$, $r=hk$, makes them equal. Applying $Rp_*$, naturality of the composition comparison and its associativity from Step 1 give $\rho_{hk}=\rho_k\circ\rho_h$. For a dense $c$, the same uniqueness identifies $e_{\operatorname{id}}$ with the identity, hence $\rho_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$; this is also clause (3) of [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement]. Only the source and intermediate compactifications were required to be dense.

source.place: Proof, Refinement isomorphisms: identity and transitivity, including a nondense final target

proof.text: For $c_1,c_2$, choose a common scheme-theoretically dense refinement $d$ with maps $h_a:d\to c_a$ using [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense], and put $\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\circ\rho_{h_1}:F_{c_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{c_2}$. This has the correct source and target because $\rho_{h_a}:F_{c_a}\to F_d$. The cited geometric lemma gives proper maps and the inverse-image-of-$X$ property even when the $c_a$ are not dense. The refinements compose with the boundary property by [det-nagata-definition-refinement].

For $c_1,c_2,c_3$ choose one common dense refinement with maps $h_1,h_2,h_3$ by the finite-family conclusion of [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]. Independence lets us use it in all three comparisons. Therefore
$$\phi_{c_3,c_2}\circ\phi_{c_2,c_1}
=(\rho_{h_3}^{-1}\rho_{h_2})(\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1})
=\rho_{h_3}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}=\phi_{c_3,c_1}.$$
For $\phi_{c,c}$ take any common dense refinement $d\to c,c$; the two projections agree by [det-nagata-refinement-morphisms] (3), or choose the same projection twice. The definition gives $\rho_h^{-1}\rho_h=\operatorname{id}_{F_c}$. This also proves the identity for a nondense $c$; taking $c$ itself as a dense refinement would not be valid then. The formulas are equalities of natural transformations, so establish every claimed clause on the stated localizing category.

lean.statement: theorem compactification_coherence_cocycle (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (_hΛ : IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ℓ Λ) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : ∃ φ : ∀ c₁ c₂ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, compactificationLocalizingCandidate Λ c₁ ≅ compactificationLocalizingCandidate Λ c₂, (∀ (c : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f) (d : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f) (h : d.obj ⟶ c) (K : (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory), IsIso (compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h K.obj)) ∧ (∀ (c₁ c₂ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f) (d : Compactification.DenseBoundaryCompactification f) (h₁ : d.obj ⟶ c₁) (h₂ : d.obj ⟶ c₂) (K : (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory), (φ c₁ c₂).hom.app K ≫ compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h₂ K.obj = compactificationRefinementComponent Λ h₁ K.obj) ∧ (∀ c : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, φ c c = Iso.refl _) ∧ (∀ c₁ c₂ c₃ : Compactification.BoundaryCompactification f, φ c₁ c₂ ≪≫ φ c₂ c₃ = φ c₁ c₃)
lean.note: The source-restricted candidate abbreviates the existing unbounded module-object composite. The canonical refinement component is Rp_* of the recorded localizingRefinementMap, followed by the inverse recorded derived compositor and the proper triangle equality. The theorem existentially supplies natural isomorphisms, with normalization against every common dense refinement, identity and cocycle equations. No density is assumed for the two compared compactifications, and no localizing-target preservation is assumed.
